rawSources.title: Corsets, crinolines and bustles: fashionable Victorian underwear

literal.prompt: Как по-французски называли отдельную нижнюю конструкцию 1870-х, которая поддерживала юбку, собранную сзади и выступавшую ниже талии?

literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A says the bustle was introduced as a distinct undergarment in the 1870s for skirts no longer worn over a crinoline, gathered up at the back and projecting below the waist; it gives tournure as its French name (L89). This matches the full stem. Crinoline is the earlier wide all-around cage (L62-L63), crinolette is a mid-1860s half-crinoline with rear half-hoops (L77-L78), and layered petticoats are an earlier volume method (L55).

literalGroups.literal: V&A называет bustle отдельной нижней конструкцией 1870-х, а её французское название — tournure (турнюр). Юбки собирали сзади и формировали выступ ниже талии складками и рюшами, часто укреплёнными конским волосом.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A directly supports bustle as a distinct 1870s undergarment, the gathered/projecting rear skirt and French name tournure (L89-L90). It says sculpted pleats and ruffles were often stiffened with horsehair (L89).

literalGroups.literal: Клеточный кринолин поддерживал широкие юбки стальными обручами, расширявшимися к подолу.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A says cage crinoline was constructed of steel hoops increasing in diameter toward the hem and supported wide skirts without burdensome petticoats (L62-L63).

literalGroups.literal: Кринолет имел плоский перед и полуобручи сзади, став переходной формой между кринолином и турнюром.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A describes the crinolette as a flat-front modified crinoline with rear half-hoops, worn from the mid-1860s as a bridge between cage crinoline and full bustle (L77-L78).

literalGroups.literal: Для турнюра создавали скульптурные складки и рюши, часто укреплённые конским волосом.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A says the bustle, also called tournure in French, used sculpted pleats and ruffles, often stiffened with horsehair (L89). This is an extra construction fact about the correct option beyond the prompt and key.

literalGroups.literal: Многослойные подъюбники придавали юбкам объём, но были тяжёлыми, жаркими и неудобными.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A says skirts gained volume from numerous layers of petticoats, including quilted styles, which were heavy, hot and unhygienic (L55); layered petticoats therefore describe an earlier alternative.
